question.value: Do the AGN host 321 GHz H2O megamasers, and how do the submillimeter masers and continuum compare with 22 GHz masers and galactic disks?

evidence.quote: Submillimeter maser emission is detected for the first time towards NGC 4945, and we present a new analysis of the submillimeter maser system in Circinus.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: 2011.0.00121.S.
All targets were observed at a rest-frame frequency of 321.226 GHz (ALMA Band 7)

claims.result: Features at 4-5 sigma, complex at ~9 sigma, 650-750 km/s
claims.finding: First submillimeter maser detection in NGC 4945

evidence.quote: the entire complex between 650 km s$^{-1}$ and 750 km s$^{-1}$ is detected at $\sim$$9 \sigma$ in integrated intensity

claims.hypothesis: 321 GHz masers trace the same sites as 22 GHz in Circinus
claims.result: Similar structure with excess at 650-750 km/s
claims.finding: 321 GHz masers may trace the disk at smaller radii

evidence.quote: the 321 GHz emission redward of 650 km s$^{-1}$ originates in the accretion disk at radii interior to where 22 GHz emission is found

limitations_admitted.value: Low SNR and ~0.5'' resolution preclude detailed characterization

evidence.quote: The low signal-to-noise in the current observations precludes any detailed characterization of this system
